text:
mia: Quick FYI — did a bring-up of reranker-compact-v2 (fp16 -> PTQ int4) on the standard rerank bench and seeing ~2.8% MRR drop on short queries (< 8 tokens). NDCG top10 shifts are smaller but noticeable.
sam: ugh, short-query regressions again :/ can you paste the eval table?
mia: pasted below, it's the condensed slice.

```
model         | MRR_all | MRR_short | NDCG10_all | NDCG10_short
-------------|---------|-----------|------------|-------------
fp16-prod     | 0.432   | 0.478     | 0.682      | 0.715
ptq-int4      | 0.420   | 0.450     | 0.674      | 0.692
delta         | -0.012  | -0.028    | -0.008     | -0.023
```

jordan: did you keep the same candidate ordering and query->doc concat? we saw ordering flips affect short queries before.
mia: yes — using the same candidate pool and ordering. Candidates are topK=50 from the bi-encoder; input format is `[query]

[doc_snippet]` (query first).
lee: did you run a run with query appended after doc (doc+query) as a quick A/B? sometimes tokenizer boundary effects on small queries.
mia: not yet, ran an ablate on prompt length and priming. I can flip order.
sam: also check embed scaling/normalization — int4 sometimes changes embedding distribution and downstream tiebreaks.
mia: good call. I'm re-running with L2-normalize embeddings before ranking. will report.
eval-bot: scheduled eval job 1734560025 started (reranker-compact-v2 | PTQ int4 | seed=42).
mia: quick note: validation set for this run was our 2025-webqa holdout (50k q/doc pairs). Could dataset selection be biasing the short-query slice?
jordan: maybe — webqa has a lot of terse queries. Do we have cross-check on the longer internal support set?
mia: yes, ran on the support-set-20k — no drop there, metric delta ~ -0.003 on MRR_short. so it's bigger on webqa.
sam: that suggests distribution sensitivity. Could be quantization amplifying tokenizer quirks on very short queries (e.g., punctuation tokens, stray whitespace). Any difference in tokenization pipeline between fp16 and ptq runs?
mia: same tokenizer version, same preproc. I did notice extra trimming step in the PTQ scoring path where we truncate to 256 tokens after serialization — shouldn't matter for short queries but i'll recheck.
lee: also check random seed & batching: continuous batching and kvcache order can affect output parity for int4. Did you freeze batch sizes?
mia: runs used batch_size=32; i'll re-run batch_size=1 deterministic to rule out batching noise.
jordan: when you re-run, add these quick experiments: (1) doc+query vs query+doc, (2) L2-normalize embeddings, (3) batch_size=1 deterministic, (4) same eval but on small curated goldset (200 queries) we use for QA.
mia: will do. timeline: re-runs queued, expecting results in ~45m.
eval-bot: job 1734560110 finished. basic checksum shows embedding mean shifted by -0.07 for int4 vs fp16 across short queries.
sam: that mean shift is actionable — maybe calibrate embedding scale with a small affine (alpha, beta) learned on a tiny calibration set. we've used that before for int8.
mia: agreed. i'll try per-dataset affine scale on webqa calibration split. also will test restoring fp16 KV order (if we can) vs ptq path.
jordan: if the issue persists after normalization and concat-order, consider trying asymmetric quant params or PTQ with per-channel scale on final projection layer. those layers are sensitive.
mia: noted. i'll add per-channel as a slower experiment.
lee: FYI — tagging #eng-ml-diagnostics and adding a short doc with the run configs and command to reproduce, so SRE/ops can replicate on dedicated infra if needed. :thumbsup:
sam: thanks. small follow-ups: please include seed, tokenizer commit hash, and candidate sampler.
mia: will add all metadata to the doc. thanks y'all.
